# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-15 (Extended v121)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Autumn Year 4, evening—crisis unfolding at Gorbeau house after 6 P.M.)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens; le Petit-Picpus convent; M. Gillenormand's residences; English provincial towns (Dunstead, Staveford, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Gulhaven, Wilwick, Wilholt). **Environmental**: Spring—frost silvering hedges, smoke flat; Summer—warm air, sparrows, bees, gulls, salt/tar scent; Autumn/Winter transition—icy breeze, snow; **Current (Autumn Year 4, evening)**: Smoke from chimneys lies flat over fields, bell for vespers rings thinly across roofs, light went early, dog barked then went quiet.

## Primary Locations
**GORBEAU HOUSE**: 50-52 Salpêtrière district. **JONDRETTE DEN**: Abject, fetid, sordid. Furniture: straw chair, infirm table, crockery, two pallets, straw beds. Walls: leprous, seamed, obscene charcoal sketches, repulsive moisture. Fireplace with brazier filled burning charcoal (glowing hot, red with blue flame), pot, broken boards, suspended rags, bird-cage. Dormer window (four broken panes). Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (sleeping woman/child, eagle, Napoleon on blue column). **Wooden panel with coarse daub painting—depicts BATTLE OF WATERLOO: sergeant rescuer (Thénardier) carrying colonel victim (Pontmercy) amid smoke and background. Marius now recognizes father in painting—"resurrection," tomb yawned, phantom risen. Marius hears cannon of Waterloo in his ears, father's blood terrifies him.** Two heaps: old iron/ropes and well-made rope-ladder with wooden rungs and two hooks. Verdigris candlestick with burning candle providing sole light. **Current state (evening, crisis unfolding)**: M. Leblanc seized moment, overturned chair with foot and table with fist, bound for window with prodigious agility before Thénardier could turn. Was half out when six robust fists seized him—three "chimney-builders" dragged him back energetically. Thénardier woman wound hands in his hair. Herculean struggle ensuing: M. Leblanc sent old man tumbling with blow to chest, overthrew two more assailants with two backward hand sweeps, held one under each knee; wretches rattling in throat beneath pressure like granite millstone. Four others seized formidable old man by both arms and back of neck, holding him doubled up. M. Leblanc now disappeared under horrible group of ruffians like wild boar beneath howling pile of dogs. **Brazier now unmasked**: Thénardier shoved aside fireplace screen, leaned against neighboring pallet, unmasking brazier full of glowing coals. Prisoner plainly sees chisel white-hot, spotted with tiny scarlet stars.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as convent assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. **Present state (Autumn Year 4)**: Cosette about thirteen/fourteen years old; appeared in Jondrette hovel as charitable visitor with M. Leblanc.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police. **Status (Autumn Year 4)**: Tall man, square face, thin firm mouth, thick gray ferocious whiskers. **Action (present, evening)**: Received report from Marius regarding Jondrette ambush. Gave Marius two small steel pistols (each loaded two balls). Instructed Marius to hide, watch through wall hole, fire when crisis reached peak. Entered hovel, purchased chisel, positioned himself for ambush. Gave key to Marius.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development, Passion, and Crisis

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years since left grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen. **Now recognized**: Thénardier depicted in Waterloo painting at Jondrette den—sergeant who rescued father at Waterloo.

**Political evolution (Winter Year 3 → Spring Year 4)**: Converted to Bonapartism and republicanism; calmed through reverie. Sympathies to humanity over nation, woman over people, idea over deed.

**Material condition (Spring Year 4)**: Gorbeau cabinet 30 francs annually; sustenance 20 sous daily; clothing 100 francs; linen 100 francs. Total: 450 francs. Earned ~700 francs yearly. Refused advancement (1,500 francs) to preserve liberty.

**Grandfather quarrel**: Violent estrangement three years ago without rapprochement.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C**: Met Courfeyrac; became good friends. Close to M. Mabeuf. Social activities: dined with Courfeyrac; breakfasted at Café Voltaire.

**Girl (Cosette)—Initial observation and passion**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty (M. Leblanc) and very young girl on Luxembourg bench daily over six months, year prior. Girl: thin, awkward, convent scholar dress. Six-month interruption. Reunion (Summer Year 3): Girl became well-dressed young maiden; wore black damask dress, white crape bonnet, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe. **First meaningful glance (Spring Year 4)**: Their glances met. Marius resolved to dress differently. Perceived she wore everyday clothes. His worship of father retreated to depths. Brain felt on fire. She appeared wholly feminine and angelic. **Love transformed him**: Vexed about dust on boots, walked like madman, ate and spoke excitedly. Combined stations behind trees with diplomacy. She bent upon Marius all reveries of virginal and passionate eye. M. Leblanc noticed something, often rose when Marius arrived, moved to adjacent bench, stared intently. **Escalation (Spring Year 4)**: Found handkerchief on bench—white, fine, perfumed, marked U. F. Marius thought "Ursule!" Kissed it, placed on heart during day, beneath lips at night. **Leg incident and jealousy**: May breeze lifted dress to height of garter. A leg of exquisite shape appeared. Marius exasperated and furious. Girl hastily thrust down dress with divinely troubled motion. **Harsh and capricious jealousy of flesh awakened in his heart.** When she passed, Marius darted sullen and ferocious glance. She gave slight backward movement: "Well, what is the matter?" Veteran in Louis XV uniform bearing soldier's cross crossed walk; Marius perceived satisfied air, struck him aged cynic addressed him fraternal wink. **Marius reached paroxysm of jealousy.** "Perhaps he was there! Perhaps he saw!"

**Disappearance and rediscovery (Summer-Autumn Year 4)**: Summer passed, autumn came, winter arrived. Neither returned to Luxembourg. Fell into black melancholy. Heaped hundred reproaches on himself. Allowed himself taken to ball at Sceaux (September) hoping to find her; did not see her; left friends, returned home on foot alone through night, weary, feverish. **Miraculous rediscovery (Autumn Year 4, afternoon before crisis)**: **Marius perceived girl in Jondrette hovel when she arrived with M. Leblanc.** "It was certainly she. Marius could hardly distinguish her through the luminous vapor which had suddenly spread before his eyes." **Marius shuddered in dismay, felt on brink of bursting into tears. His heart palpitated; seemed to him he had lost his soul and just found it again.** During entire visit, Marius lived in ecstasy; eyes remained fixed on girl; heart seized and wholly enveloped her. **He devoured her with his eyes. Could not believe divine creature was in midst of vile creatures in that monstrous lair. Seemed to him he beheld humming-bird in midst of toads.**

**Crisis of conscience (evening, crisis unfolding)**: Everything depended on Marius. Unknown to themselves, he held all beings in his hand. If he fired pistol, M. Leblanc saved, Thénardier lost; if he did not fire, M. Leblanc sacrificed. Remorse awaited him either case. What should he choose? Be false to most imperious souvenirs, all solemn vows, most sacred duty, most venerated text? Ignore father's testament or allow perpetration of crime? On one hand heard "his Ursule" supplicating for her father; on other, colonel commending Thénardier to his care. **He felt he was going mad. His knees gave way beneath him.** Had not time for deliberation—scene hastening to catastrophe like whirlwind sweeping him away. **He was on verge of swooning.** **Marius regained some measure of control. Last possibility of doubt vanished. Certainly was Thénardier of the will.** Marius shuddered at reproach of ingratitude directed against his father, which he was on point of so fatally justifying. **His perplexity was redoubled.** **But now, with Waterloo painting recognized, critical realization: father once saved by Thénardier at Waterloo—sergeant rescued colonel. Yet M. Leblanc now victim of Thénardier's ambush. Moral obligation to both: honor father's will (protect Thénardier) AND prevent crime against innocent man and Cosette's father. Crisis of conscience at absolute peak.**

## The Jondrette Family and Ambush Plot—Active Phase (Autumn Year 4, Evening)

**Thénardier's nature and transformation (revealed)**: Contains two men—ferocious man and adroit man. In excess of triumph over prey brought down and not stirring, ferocious man prevailed. When victim struggled and tried to resist, adroit man reappeared and took upper hand. M. Leblanc's desperate attempt calmed him rather than exasperating. **Now adopting polished, measured demeanor**: Thénardier rose unpretending manner, went to fireplace. **Marius found it difficult to recognize in that polished smile of man in official life the almost bestial mouth which had been foaming moment before; gazed with amazement at fantastic and alarming metamorphosis; felt as man might feel who should behold tiger converted into lawyer.** Thénardier's language now stamped with moderated, subdued insolence and crafty insolence, reserved and almost choice. In that rascal, who had been nothing but robber short time previously, one now felt "the man who had studied for the priesthood."

**Current negotiation (evening, after binding)**: Thénardier stated: "We can come to an understanding. Let us arrange this matter in an amicable way. I was wrong to lose my temper just now, I don't know what I was thinking of, I went a great deal too far, I said extravagant things. For example, because you are a millionnaire, I told you that I exacted money, a lot of money. That would not be reasonable. Mon Dieu, in spite of your riches, you have expenses of your own—who has not? I don't want to ruin you. I am not a greedy fellow, after all. I don't want to make myself ridiculous. I'm taking things into consideration and making a sacrifice on my side. I only want two hundred thousand francs."

**M. Leblanc's composure**: M. Leblanc had appeared watching and following all Thénardier's movements while Thénardier, blinded by rage, stalked back and forth in den with full confidence door was guarded, holding unarmed man fast, being armed himself, having nine against one (female Thénardier counted as one man). Despite being bound with ropes, surrounded with executioners, half plunged in grave closing upon him moment by moment, in presence of Thénardier's wrath and sweetness, M. Leblanc remained impassive. **Marius could not refrain from admiring superbly melancholy visage at such moment.** Here evidently was soul inaccessible to terror, which did not know meaning of despair. One of those men who command amazement in desperate circumstances. Extreme as crisis was, inevitable as catastrophe, nothing here of agony of drowning man opening horror-filled eyes under water. **The silence preserved by prisoner, that precaution carried to point of forgetting all anxiety for own life, that resistance opposed to first impulse of nature (to utter cry)—all this now troubled Marius, affected him with painful astonishment.**

## Friends of the A B C and Criminal Underground

**Friends of the A B C**: Secret society in embryonic state. Meetings back room Café Musain. Members: Enjolras, Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—_Abaissé_, the debased (the people).

**Patron-Minette**: Criminal association members Babet, Gueulemer, Claquesous, Montparnasse. **Gueulemer**: Six feet high, Hercules. **Claquesous**: He was night. Ventriloquist. **Thénardier**: Originally innkeeper; revealed as sergeant who rescued Colonel Pontmercy at Waterloo; now orchestrating ambush at Gorbeau.

## English Provincial Towns: Mundane Activities and Births (Autumn Year 4)

**Pelde Stenson and Davus Stenworth**: Daughter born, named Dalis Stenworth. Family lived in Torton. Pelde counted coins twice, came up penny short. Davus fell asleep in chair before fire. Pelde mended torn sleeve by window, said little. Pelde walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Pelde spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. **Pelde hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step.**

**Yera Stenworth**: Hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Told "You look tired," by Pelde Stenworth, did not deny it.

**Dalis Stenworth/Dalis (daughter)**: Predicted rain wrongly. Laughed at story nobody else found funny. Hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step.

**Harine Lindmere and Pelde**: Talked of nothing much—weather, harvest, lame horse. Harine asked "Will it rain, do you think?" Dalis only shrugged. Road all ruts and puddles after thaw.

**General conditions**: Frost silvered hedges overnight. Gulls quarreled over heap of fish heads by steps. Rain threatened since morning but held off. Baker's boy late again; line at oven grew long. Someone chalked crooked sun on wall of forge. **Kadrek went along to live in Wilholt.** **Only daughter of Zalis Corrley left Torton and settled in Wilholt.**
